kept.text: CQRS stands for Command Query Responsibility Segregation.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: At its heart is the notion that you can use a different model to update information than the model you use to read information.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: For some situations, this separation can be valuable, but beware that for most systems CQRS adds risky complexity.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: The change that CQRS introduces is to split that conceptual model into separate models for update and display, which it refers to as Command and Query respectively following the vocabulary of CommandQuerySeparation.
kept.subject: separate command model

kept.text: The rationale is that for many problems, particularly in more complicated domains, having the same conceptual model for commands and queries leads to a more complex model that does neither well.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: By separate models we most commonly mean different object models, probably running in different logical processes, perhaps on separate hardware.
kept.subject: separate command model

kept.text: If they initiate a change that change is routed to the separate command model for processing, the resulting change is communicated to the query model to render the updated state.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: The in-memory models may share the same database, in which case the database acts as the communication between the two models.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: However they may also use separate databases, effectively making the query-side's database into a real-time ReportingDatabase.
kept.subject: ReportingDatabase

kept.text: The two models might not be separate object models, it could be that the same objects have different interfaces for their command side and their query side, rather like views in relational databases.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: But usually when I hear of CQRS, they are clearly separate models.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: CQRS is suited to complex domains, the kind that also benefit from Domain-Driven Design.
kept.subject: CQRS

kept.text: Like any pattern, CQRS is useful in some places, but not in others.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: CQRS is a significant mental leap for all concerned, so shouldn't be tackled unless the benefit is worth the jump.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: In particular CQRS should only be used on specific portions of a system (a BoundedContext in DDD lingo) and not the system as a whole.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: In this way of thinking, each Bounded Context needs its own decisions on how it should be modeled.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: So far I see benefits in two directions.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: Firstly is that a few complex domains may be easier to tackle by using CQRS.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: I must stress, however, that such suitability for CQRS is very much the minority case.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: Usually there's enough overlap between the command and query sides that sharing a model is easier.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: Using CQRS on a domain that doesn't match it will add complexity, thus reducing productivity and increasing risk.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: The other main benefit is in handling high performance applications.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: CQRS allows you to separate the load from reads and writes allowing you to scale each independently.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: If your application sees a big disparity between reads and writes this is very handy.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: If your domain isn't suited to CQRS, but you have demanding queries that add complexity or performance problems, remember that you can still use a ReportingDatabase.
kept.subject: ReportingDatabase

kept.text: CQRS uses a separate model for all queries.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: With a reporting database you still use your main system for most queries, but offload the more demanding ones to the reporting database.
kept.subject: ReportingDatabase

kept.text: Despite these benefits, you should be very cautious about using CQRS.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: Many information systems fit well with the notion of an information base that is updated in the same way that it's read, adding CQRS to such a system can add significant complexity.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: I've certainly seen cases where it's made a significant drag on productivity, adding an unwarranted amount of risk to the project, even in the hands of a capable team.
kept.subject: When to use it

kept.text: So while CQRS is a pattern that's good to have in the toolbox, beware that it is difficult to use well and you can easily chop off important bits if you mishandle it.
kept.subject: When to use it
